newsitem.title: USA: Key witness grilled on bombing testimony.
newsitem.headline: Key witness grilled on bombing testimony.

text.p: Key prosecution witness Lori Fortier denied on Wednesday that she agreed to testify against Oklahoma bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh in order to stay out of jail.

During cross-examination by defence attorney Stephen Jones, Fortier, wife of McVeigh's Army buddy Michael Fortier, also denied Jones' claims that she hoped to make a fortune from selling her version of McVeigh's alleged plot to blow up the Oklahoma City federal building.
"I never wanted to sell my story," Fortier said.
McVeigh is accused of planning and carrying out the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City, killing 168 people. If convicted, he faces the death penalty.

Fortier, who testified on Tuesday that McVeigh told her of his plans to blow up the federal building to avenge the government siege of the Branch Davidian compound in Waco, Texas two years earlier, said she initially thought McVeigh was innocent.
However, she later changed her story when co-defendant Terry Nichols was arrested. She was later promised immunity from prosecution.

Branch Davidian cult leader David Koresh and about 80 followers died in flames after a botched FBI raid on their Waco compound on April 19, 1993. Since then Waco has been a rallying cry of the right-wing militia movement and it was on the two-year anniversary of the Waco raid that the Oklahoma City bombing occurred.
Jones, seeking to damage her credibility, asked Fortier if she felt responsible for the deadly attack.
"All you had to do to prevent the death of 168 people was to pick up the telephone?" he asked.
"Yes," she said in a weak voice.

Michael Fortier has entered into a plea agreement, admitting he knew McVeigh had planned the bombing but did nothing to stop it. Michael Fortier is in federal custody, facing up to 23 years in prison and is also expected to be a key witness for the prosecution.

During cross examination, Lorie Fortier said the couple did not hope to profit by selling their story but she did admit to hearing a conversation between her husband and his family about how the couple could make money by telling their story.
McVeigh stayed with the Fortiers at their trailer home in Kingman, Arizona, during several visits, Lori Fortier testified.

After McVeigh was charged with the bombing, Lori Fortier wrote a news release, which was never issued, claiming their friend was not capable of the bombing and that he was being treated unfairly by the news media, which she called "money hungry vultures."
"It truly sickens me when I see my friend's face, yes, friend's face portrayed on the front of Time magazine as the face of terror," she wrote in her statement.
She testified on Tuesday, however, that she had become frightened of McVeigh before the bombing when he was living in Arizona for a short time.
